statusRule: LIVE requires current runtime verification for the intended audience. No claim in this shard is marked LIVE. Default-off implementation remains IMPLEMENTED with explicit limits.

claims.claim: Invitation admission is implemented for new accounts; existing accounts retain access.
claims.safeNarration: Entry follows the current invitation rules.
claims.safeDepiction: Show actual current signed-out/invite UI; do not promise open access.
limits: Current production admission policy must be separately observed.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: A new street begins in Docks with a small gameplay-cash balance and no respect. Core actions include jobs, training, bank use and building income sources.
claims.safeNarration: You begin at the docks. Take a job. Train. Decide what to risk and what to protect.
claims.safeDepiction: Real character creation and one issued action/result; label isolated seeded build.
limits: Currency shown here is gameplay cash, not dollars of withdrawable value.
Do not imply a beginner instantly commands a Family or completes the gated world arc.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Jobs consume resources and can cause jail; heat feeds law pressure. Banking has a transit exposure window and is not death-proof.
claims.safeNarration: Every useful move has a cost: time, resources, heat, or exposure.
claims.safeDepiction: Pair a real job with visible costs and result; bank protection must retain in-transit state when applicable.
limits: Do not call bank cash permanently safe.
Use actual runtime costs, not narrator-invented values.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: The six careers are The Gun, The Ledger, The Kitchen, The Wheel, The Shadow and The Ring. Each has an advantage, a handicap and favored/disfavored trades.
claims.safeNarration: Six Paths change how you work—and what you are bad at.
claims.safeDepiction: Six exact names; selected path card shows perk plus drawback.
limits: Choice is level/cost gated; do not depict Path as a free character-creation class.
The Ledger career is distinct from The Ledger Season Pass.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Gun favors combat/contracts at cost of goods sales; Ledger favors business/trade at cost of street combat; Kitchen favors production/deal heat at cost of jail; Wheel speeds convoys but slows cooking; Shadow speeds searches but weakens contests; Ring strengthens contests but raises healing cost.
claims.safeNarration: Specialists need each other because an edge in one loop can be a weakness in another.
claims.safeDepiction: Use scope-specific icons; no magic powers or unrestricted class exclusives.
limits: Use qualitative scope in narration; exact balance values only from captured current cards.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Docks, Neon Mile, Old Foundry, Brick Yards, Canal Row and Cathedral Hill have different gameplay advantages. Travel has a cost.
claims.safeNarration: Where you work matters. The city changes the terms.
claims.safeDepiction: Actual district map plus one relevant modifier and travel action.
limits: Do not equate game district control with liquidity ownership.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Upgradeable fronts accrue game cash with caps/upkeep and exposure to raids/takeover; the Kitchen supports cooking, collection, dealing and hired sellers.
claims.safeNarration: Your operation can keep working while you are away. Its upkeep and risks do not disappear.
claims.safeDepiction: Business collect/upkeep and kitchen job clock; cash marked as gameplay cash.
limits: No cash-to-OMR laundering route.
No unlimited passive income or real-money yield claim.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Owned cars can be boosted, repaired, fenced or melted for ammunition under applicable gates. A separate workshop crafts gear/ammo from crates and cash; World Graph salvage is a different material flow.
claims.safeNarration: A car can be transport, a trade, or the input to your next move.
claims.safeDepiction: Show the chosen actual route: melt to ammo OR World Graph salvage to materials, not an invented merged output.
limits: Confirm exact eligible vehicle and generated outputs at capture time.
Never animate arbitrary scenery into owned inventory.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Ownable boats run maritime routes with interdiction, piracy, upgrades and consensual rendezvous. Active boats are gameplay assets.
claims.safeNarration: On the water, cargo has a route—and somebody else may want it.
claims.safeDepiction: Real port board and voyage clock; depict rival risk without revealing private manifests.
limits: Extracted boats cannot work while on-chain; production extraction remains unverified/dormant per docs.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Cars use auctions; goods trade at district pickups with trunk limits; buy orders escrow payment. Markets do not teleport freight past convoy rules.
claims.safeNarration: Making the trade is only part of the job. The goods still have to move.
claims.safeDepiction: Listing to pickup requirement to convoy; use same item identity.
limits: This player market is separate from the current on-chain market and the campaign Black Market world state.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Source includes racing, fighting, casino/card games, stables, skills/trades, fixers, law/courts, prison and loan-sharking systems.
claims.safeNarration: A city full of side games becomes a city full of competing priorities.
claims.safeDepiction: Brief authentic UI collage; named activity only if its UI is actually captured.
limits: No all-features-live inference; no financial returns framing for gambling.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Persistent Crews are account-bound small mutual-aid groups with chat, member boards and breakable non-aggression. They survive character death; no shared Crew treasury or turf authority.
claims.safeNarration: A Crew is the small circle you choose to keep close.
claims.safeDepiction: Actual Crew membership/invitation and chat; no invented communal inventory.
limits: A heist crew, Kitchen hired crew, persistent Crew and Family are distinct.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Families have treasury, roles, wars, turf and collective standing; boss/underboss authority matters.
claims.safeNarration: A Family turns individual ambition into a shared operation—with someone accountable for the decisions.
claims.safeDepiction: Actual Family board with visible role and treasury permissions.
limits: Current membership matters; authority is not transferable merely by knowing a name.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Leader stakes and plans; members fill specialist roles; leader executes; shared success/failure affects participants.
claims.safeNarration: The plan needs a crew whose skills fit the job. One missing role changes the decision.
claims.safeDepiction: Real role seats with missing member, join, execution and actual result.
limits: Do not conflate these ordinary heists with default-off Family world operations.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: A heist member can secretly inform; the job is blown. Other members see that somebody talked, not the informer identity. The jail treatment includes the rat to avoid identification from the roster.
claims.safeNarration: The job can fail because somebody talked. The city does not hand you their name.
claims.safeDepiction: Capture the anonymous outcome; actor dramatization is not proof identifying a player.
limits: No psychic rat detection.
Do not use the separate Campaign Informant evidence as proof of this heist rat.
Do not depict rat escaping jail while everyone else is imprisoned.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Freight uses an actual journey clock and can be ambushed. Route/value band are public; manifest and guard tier are not. Turf contributes protection and destination control can impose tolls.
claims.safeNarration: The route is visible. The cargo is not. You decide how much protection the trip deserves.
claims.safeDepiction: Public banded route against owner-only manifest shown as separate viewpoints.
limits: Do not reveal a rival full manifest or guard tier through a public board.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: District control is economically relevant to Family rackets; contested holdings use hidden stakes, timing and adjacency.
claims.safeNarration: Territory is a position you defend, with costs the whole Family feels.
claims.safeDepiction: Public map/control and authorized own commitment; keep rivals sealed bids hidden.
limits: Game territory never implies a right to withdraw LP principal.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Seated Families vote on server-wide weekly decrees. Membership/rank and office control voting rights.
claims.safeNarration: Power reaches beyond one block. Families can shape the rules other players face.
claims.safeDepiction: Actual decree ballot or active decree; no invented vote or result.
limits: Do not imply voting changes arbitrary game rules or grants unrestricted treasury/contract authority.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Canonical items, resources, relationships and world state are connected through authoritative services. Item custody/provenance is conserved; newer world adapters are default off.
claims.safeNarration: An item has a history. An action can leave a consequence other players encounter.
claims.safeDepiction: Same authorized item ID through owned inventory, contribution and recorded consequence.
limits: Label gated world content DEVELOPMENT PILOT.
Provenance is not automatically public and is not NFT export.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Original discoveries, permitted sharing and current ACL/membership checks determine evidence use; copies do not create independent sources.
claims.safeNarration: You can share what you discovered. You cannot manufacture a second witness by copying it.
claims.safeDepiction: Two actual authorized source cards or deliberately redacted proof of distinct contributors.
limits: Default-off knowledge/sharing flags and cohort gate.
Distinct accounts are not proof of distinct humans.
Do not disclose puzzle answers or hidden source requirements.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Mystery discoveries, owned items, authenticated information and authored prerequisites can unlock crafting or story actions. Recipes consume canonical inputs.
claims.safeNarration: Sometimes the missing ingredient is something another player knows.
claims.safeDepiction: Known recipe blocker plus authorized discovery/share, then actual recipe readiness; hide the solution.
limits: New core-progression content defaults off.
Mystery evidence is not automatically trusted Coordination knowledge.
Never imply infinite AI-generated murder mysteries.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Default-off Family operations combine roles, promises, actual contributions, escrow, approval and atomic world resolution. Seats accept 2–8 distinct accounts by definition.
claims.safeNarration: A promise is not a contribution. The operation waits for what the people and the plan actually require.
claims.safeDepiction: Missing/fulfilled contribution states, each owner acting, officer approval and authorized executor.
limits: Do not turn one pilot four-seat count into a universal rule.
Officer assignment cannot spend another player inventory.
Execution requires the defined executor role plus officer/current-authority checks.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Commands are issued from current visible projections and revalidate authority/requirements when executed; irreversible choices and relevant consequential actions carry confirmations.
claims.safeNarration: You see the move, its cost and its consequences before you commit.
claims.safeDepiction: Actual command card and matching confirmation/result; no invented API interface.
limits: Gated world command availability is separate from ordinary actions.
Not every harmless action requires a confirmation.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Default-off Director observes canonical conditions and selects bounded authored situations. It cannot mint evidence/assets, resolve operations or move money.
claims.safeNarration: The city can respond to what players actually changed.
claims.safeDepiction: Previous actual consequence to an eligible authored opportunity, labeled development pilot.
limits: Not an unrestricted autonomous content generator.
No autonomous NPC economy adapter is admitted in the pilot.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Disabled implementation connects shipment-route outcomes, market infrastructure and investigation through actual prerequisites. History reveals only authorized states; unknown actors and causes remain absent.
claims.safeNarration: One crew changes a route. Another encounters the consequences.
claims.safeDepiction: Use a captured eligible connected branch; label acting as dramatization and UI as dev build.
limits: Do not force every terminal branch into a new opportunity.
No automatic supply-to-OMR-price causal chain.
No hidden solution or investigator-private clue in public montage.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: The campaign Informant can corroborate public disclosure or record failure/uncertainty; it does not name a guilty player or prove betrayal.
claims.safeNarration: Evidence can prove what happened without proving why somebody did it.
claims.safeDepiction: Public/disputed/unknown indicators; no suspect convicted by AI.
limits: Do not conflate this with actual ordinary-heist informing.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: HTTP API, machine-readable rules, MCP proxy and Agent Turn support agents. Server-issued actions are revalidated against actual state.
claims.safeNarration: An agent can use the same game rules and interfaces a player works through.
claims.safeDepiction: Actual authorized Agent Turn read/action/result; disclose automation.
limits: MCP/source presence alone does not prove current installation or live server availability.
Human-only reward exclusions still apply.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Owner-operated Agent Alpha is finite and allowlisted; it excludes PvP, borrowing, human faucets, wallets, mint, withdrawals and arbitrary mutations. Agent Turn exploration grants no execution authority.
claims.safeNarration: You can delegate a bounded set of routine moves. Permission and game rules still define the boundary.
claims.safeDepiction: Show owner-started action budget and actual allowed action; never stage private-key handling.
limits: Do not claim every agent move is manually approved.
Do not claim general agents lack capabilities solely because the reference runner excludes them.
World Graph and authored-content actions are direct-only, not autonomous Agent Act.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: The local dirty worktree contains a provider-neutral scoped adviser with proposals requiring player confirmation. It is absent from canonical main; native Muse compatibility and integration with latest campaigns are unverified.
claims.safeNarration: An adviser interface is being explored; its proposals return to the player for approval.
claims.safeDepiction: Only separately labeled LOCAL PROTOTYPE footage; prefer omission from present-tense flagship feature claims.
limits: Local evidence: docs/agent-gateway-capabilities.md:11-31,48-52; docs/agent-gateway-muse.md:101-125; src/integrations/muse/manifest.js:2-11.
Never combine local adviser UI with latest campaign data and imply executed integration.
The canonical dynasty Consigliere office is a relationship between player accounts, not proof of this AI adviser.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Death ends the character; the account continues through an heir. Many street assets/cash/stats are lost; specified account-level legacy survives.
claims.safeNarration: Your character can die. Your account and parts of your legacy continue—but the next life does not inherit everything.
claims.safeDepiction: Separate dead character from continuing account; show actual estate disposition and heir.
limits: Remaining OMR is subject to loot/death rules; no claim all balances are safe.
Do not imply all inventory, business ownership or previous character authority transfers.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Seasons last 28 days with progression resets/prestige and Family competition phases; season records and account legacy persist under their own rules.
claims.safeNarration: The season closes the books. It does not erase every mark your people made.
claims.safeDepiction: Season phase/status and actual prior record; separate character reset from Family history.
limits: Do not say everything resets or nothing resets.
Seasonal rewards depend on current subsystem eligibility/funding.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Source implements item extraction/redemption rails, but docs say production extraction dormant until verified. Extracted items are inert in gameplay; eligibility differs by asset.
claims.safeNarration: The extraction design trades use in the city for custody outside it. Availability must be verified separately.
claims.safeDepiction: If retained, explicit INACTIVE EXTRACTION PREVIEW; show no real successful transaction unless evidenced.
limits: Do not imply every inventory item is an NFT.
Wallet link and character mint are prerequisite gates, not proof the rail is active.
Exported safety means outside specified game losses, not universal wallet/security immunity.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Latest inspected readiness work retains unmet qualification proof and explicitly authorizes no cohort admission; source and scoped tests are not live deployment.
claims.safeNarration: This footage shows an implemented development build.
claims.safeDepiction: Persistent development status on gated demonstrations; no PLAY NOW/open-access claim derived from tests.
limits: Sep20 frozen blocked result is historical; latest readiness work also withholds clearance.
Root must separately verify intended production audience and activation before changing a claim to LIVE.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.claim: Open-ended AI content generation and autonomous NPC economy adapters remain beyond the bounded authored Director pilot.
claims.safeNarration: Omit from present-tense feature narration.
claims.safeDepiction: If essential, clearly separated future-design card.
limits: Older Coordination README understates implemented Family adapters; do not use its blanket later-phase wording to erase current code.
claims.liveVerification: Not verified for an intended production audience in this audit.

claims.statement: The current market is implemented source. Repository documentation and retained deployments do not establish that this exact market, withdrawal or RWA pipeline is operating on September 29.
claims.safeNarration: The implemented market has separate rules for trading, liquidity and Family fee rights.
claims.safeDepiction: Use a legible chapter label: IMPLEMENTED RULES · ACTIVATION UNVERIFIED. Do not fabricate wallet receipts, transactions, balances or an open trading interface.

sources.note: Historical September 11 dormant snapshot only; not current market activation or a fresh live read.

publicationBlockers: No current source-matched activation evidence was available to this shard. The historical deployment record must not be repurposed as clearance.

claims.statement: Game cash, the server's in-game OMR ledger and wallet ERC-20 OMR are separate value domains with different custody and loss rules.
claims.safeNarration: Three balances. Three rules. Game cash. In-game OMR. Wallet OMR.
claims.safeDepiction: Three labeled compartments; game cash explicitly says GAME CURRENCY. No dollar-to-dollar peg and no merged total.
publicationBlockers: Capture balance labels from the approved development build; redact identifying account/wallet information.
avoid: every in-game OMR credit is a wallet token

claims.statement: The Window spends in-game OMR for game cash from a funded till, with opening and account-limit checks. Cash has no general reverse route into OMR. An insufficient till refuses without taking OMR.
claims.safeNarration: The funded Window moves OMR into game cash. The arrow does not run backwards.
claims.safeDepiction: Single arrow IN-GAME OMR → FUNDED WINDOW → GAME CASH. Show till availability as a condition, never as an exchange-rate peg.
publicationBlockers: Do not show a currently open Window without checking the capture build's actual board and funding.

claims.statement: OMR supports selected equipment/upgrades, career changes, intelligence/protection, estates, subscriptions, selected service alternatives and access stakes. Some benefits are mechanically consequential, not all cosmetic.
claims.safeNarration: In-game OMR buys selected equipment, access and services.
claims.safeDepiction: Show two verified actions or gates with current requirements. A bought item can affect gameplay; do not label all OMR utility cosmetic.
publicationBlockers: Use actual item/service requirements from the pinned build. Do not imply a wallet holding automatically unlocks an in-game stake gate.
avoid: wallet balance automatically counts as a game stake

claims.statement: Career OMR awards are limited once-per-account internal credits. Daily and other pools are funded transfers under eligibility rules. Internal credits do not automatically create ERC-20 tokens or establish immediate withdrawal backing.
claims.safeNarration: Missions award limited game OMR; funded pools can distribute rewards. That is not an automatic wallet payout.
claims.safeDepiction: Mission receipt remains in the IN-GAME OMR compartment; a separate locked withdrawal gate appears before wallet custody.
publicationBlockers: Do not present historical ledger vocabulary as permission to emit new rewards. Any displayed amount must come from source/capture.
avoid: every mission mints a wallet token

claims.statement: Many in-game OMR spends recycle into backend Desk inventory rather than destroying ERC-20 supply. Window OMR is split between Family funding and Desk. Backend Desk inventory is not the market controller's Desk liquidity compartment.
claims.safeNarration: Many game spends recycle OMR. They do not permanently burn token supply.
claims.safeDepiction: Spend receipt flows to REUSABLE GAME INVENTORY; never into a fire, shrinking total-supply counter or directly into the market controller's Desk.
publicationBlockers: Do not connect the two different Desk accounts merely because they share a label.
avoid: backend spending directly opens a liquidity position

claims.statement: Canonical Hook base sell charge is 9%: developer 2%, RWA allocation 1.6%, community 2.4%, POL 3%; bounded surge is 0–1% to stability. Ordinary LP fees are additional. Normal buys after the configured opening window have no Hook buy tax. Fee asset follows settlement and can be ETH or OMR.
claims.safeNarration: The Hook routes canonical trading fees to separate destinations.
claims.safeDepiction: Only if rates are useful: 9% BASE SELL CHARGE with four additive shares and a separate +0–1% STABILITY line. Label CODE POLICY, LP FEES ADDITIONAL; no selected live LP rate.
publicationBlockers: Current deployment/runtime match, configuration, actual funding, authorized integration and activation evidence are required before describing this mechanism as live.
avoid: all trades everywhere pay this charge

claims.statement: Protocol liquidity uses segregated actual capital and constrained positions. Core is intended to receive POL funding; action, episode and lifetime limits bind use. Governance has defined principal-recovery powers. This is not a guaranteed floor or a redeemable share of reserves.
claims.safeNarration: The market uses separate, funded liquidity budgets.
claims.safeDepiction: Core liquidity is a finite box, with principal separate from earned fees. Use a range diagram only if assets cannot appear from nothing.
publicationBlockers: Current deployment/runtime match, configuration, actual funding, authorized integration and activation evidence are required before describing this mechanism as live.

claims.statement: Inventory bonds reserve already-held OMR for a buyer paying ETH, then release it through linear vesting. They do not mint and cannot promise more than funded inventory. Code bounds are not selected commercial terms.
claims.safeNarration: Inventory bonds sell OMR already held, released over time.
claims.safeDepiction: Finite OMR inventory → RESERVED FOR BUYER → VESTED CLAIM. ETH proceeds feed a separately labeled recovery-capital destination, not the buyer's yield.
publicationBlockers: Current deployment/runtime match, configuration, actual funding, authorized integration and activation evidence are required before describing this mechanism as live.
avoid: public offer with invented discount or vesting period

claims.statement: The commitment vault requires an eligible canonical PositionManager NFT and measured useful liquidity; campaign rewards are prefunded ETH, bounded by campaign/position conditions and available funds. A token balance alone is not an eligible LP position.
claims.safeNarration: LP rewards need qualifying positions and funded campaigns.
claims.safeDepiction: POSITION NFT → QUALIFICATION + TIME → FINITE ETH CAMPAIGN. Do not connect every wallet OMR balance to this reward path.
publicationBlockers: Current deployment/runtime match, configuration, actual funding, authorized integration and activation evidence are required before describing this mechanism as live.
avoid: passive OMR holding earns LP rewards
staking OMR is the same as committing an LP NFT

claims.statement: The original depositor can retrieve a mature LP NFT under the specified oracle/pause/budget failures; credited rewards are separate. Return of the position does not guarantee its economic value or original asset composition.
claims.safeNarration: At maturity, the position can return even if the reward budget is empty.
claims.safeDepiction: Two controls: RETURN MATURE POSITION and CLAIM CREDITED REWARD. Never show an unchanging fiat balance or a guarantee seal.
publicationBlockers: Current deployment/runtime match, configuration, actual funding, authorized integration and activation evidence are required before describing this mechanism as live.
avoid: reward pool guarantees original LP value

claims.statement: A solver supplies its own collateral for an atomic cross-pool trade. Successful execution requires positive realized profit after trading charges; a configured share of profit goes to reserves. Gas and failed transactions can still cost money.
claims.safeNarration: Successful arbitrage contributes a share of actual profit.
claims.safeDepiction: SOLVER CAPITAL → COMPLETED PROFITABLE CYCLE → PROFIT SPLIT. Never route gross turnover or all solver capital to treasury; no endless-profit animation.
publicationBlockers: Current deployment/runtime match, configuration, actual funding, authorized integration and activation evidence are required before describing this mechanism as live.
avoid: all price differences are guaranteed earnings
reserve share comes from gross notional

claims.statement: Families or syndicates can hold seasonal rights to future funded fees from designated LP positions. Historical credited fees remain with their beneficiaries. Protocol principal remains controlled separately.
claims.safeNarration: Families compete for designated liquidity-fee rights. The pool's principal stays protocol-controlled.
claims.safeDepiction: One specified Turf position emits ACTUAL EARNED FEES toward a Family treasury; a solid boundary retains LP PRINCIPAL. Other pool fees do not automatically join the Family stream.
publicationBlockers: Current deployment/runtime match, configuration, actual funding, authorized integration and activation evidence are required before describing this mechanism as live.
avoid: take the docks and seize the whole pool
all trading fees pay your Family

claims.statement: A siege allocates actual funded fee escrow and future ownership through typed authenticated game outcomes. The server adjudicates combat; the contract checks the authorized result and conservation/replay rules.
claims.safeNarration: The contest changes who receives funded fees; it does not let a Family empty the pool.
claims.safeDepiction: Actual accrued fee escrow splits only after a verified outcome. Overlay GAME ADJUDICATION → AUTHORIZED SETTLEMENT, not fully onchain combat.
publicationBlockers: Current deployment/runtime match, configuration, actual funding, authorized integration and activation evidence are required before describing this mechanism as live.
avoid: officers can rewrite prior earned claims

claims.statement: The initial 100-million-OMR mint is not an immutable supply cap. The owner can appoint or disable a minter; a designated minter can mint. Inventory-funded bond sales do not remove that separate authority.
claims.safeNarration: The token retains controlled mint authority.
claims.safeDepiction: If supply is discussed, say INITIAL SUPPLY, NOT HARD CAP. Show GOVERNANCE → MINTER AUTHORITY; no permanent fixed-supply stamp.
publicationBlockers: Current minter address and actual circulating supply require fresh chain evidence. Do not infer present mint configuration or distribution from source.
avoid: bond inventory makes the token permanently non-inflationary

claims.statement: OMR withdrawal requires a qualifying account, valid destination, sufficient liquid in-game OMR and configured active signing/chain services. Gross ledger debit differs from net voucher. Funding shortages can queue requests; claims transfer existing chain tokens.
claims.safeNarration: Withdrawal needs eligibility, backing and an active chain rail.
claims.safeDepiction: IN-GAME OMR → ELIGIBILITY / FUNDED RESERVE / FEES → WALLET OMR. Queue shown as PENDING, never as settled.
publicationBlockers: No withdrawals or claims are authorized for production capture. Current deployment activation/funding not verified.
avoid: signed voucher equals completed wallet transfer

claims.statement: Current documented withdrawal default is a 2% toll plus a fresh-balance surcharge beginning at 50% and declining to zero over 48 hours. Additive lot-based calculation; newest balances are considered first. Market-sale fees are separate. Canceling an unsigned queue returns net, not the already paid toll.
claims.safeNarration: Fresh balances cost more to extract.
claims.safeDepiction: Freshness slider is an illustration of documented rules, not a live quote; label WITHDRAWAL FEES with EXAMPLE / CHECK CURRENT QUOTE. Avoid numerical example in the master unless needed.
publicationBlockers: Current operational overrides and actual quote must be checked before using a numeric user outcome.
avoid: after 48 hours every exit is free
withdrawal tax is market sell tax
wallet-only holdings automatically pay game withdrawal surcharge

claims.statement: Eligible gear, cars and boats have class-token export rails; separate StreetDeed and Dynasty portrait rails have different rights. Exported gear/vehicles become inert in gameplay. Confirmed reimport burns the exported token and restores game ownership. Not every World Graph item is exportable.
claims.safeNarration: Eligible gear and vehicles can leave too. Once exported, they stop working in-game.
claims.safeDepiction: One eligible item leaves ACTIVE LOADOUT and enters WALLET; original gameplay slot becomes unavailable. Separate receipt for confirmed reimport. No cloned active item.
publicationBlockers: Eligibility, contract caps, signer configuration and actual settled export require per-class evidence. Use a dry development UI or labeled diagram, not a fake mint receipt.
avoid: every token is a unique immutable rarity

claims.statement: Eligible combat can loot liquid/unbonding and staked in-game OMR under current rules; death then applies additional duty to remaining liquid/unbonding balances. Locks do not make game stake immune. An unrelated external wallet's OMR is outside this game-balance mutation.
claims.safeNarration: Your game balance can be lost in the city. Combat cannot seize an unrelated external wallet.
claims.safeDepiction: Highlight risk only inside the GAME CUSTODY box. External wallet label says OUTSIDE GAME COMBAT, not SAFE FROM ALL RISK.
publicationBlockers: If quoting loss rates, identify them as current base rules subject to applicable eligibility and modifiers; no unconditional example for every death.
avoid: staked game OMR cannot be looted
game death drains a connected wallet

claims.statement: The broad Stock Machine ambition is approved-asset selection, bounded purchase, allocations and Stock Token delivery. Supporting modules are implemented, but the acquisition constellation is not a completed autonomous purchase service; its authority's unpause always reverts and execution scaffolding does not complete the purchase path.
claims.safeNarration: The RWA ambition includes approved Stock Tokens, Commission choices and eligible allocations. That complete pipeline is not established live.
claims.safeDepiction: Dashed PLANNED CONNECTIONS from APPROVED ASSET → PURCHASE → CUSTODY → ELIGIBLE ALLOCATION → DELIVERY. Stages do not animate as settled transactions.
publicationBlockers: Complete and activate the selected acquisition path, approved adapter/oracle, custody, eligibility, allocation and delivery dependencies before claiming a live end-to-end service.
avoid: RWA allocation alone proves a buy
a registry entry is a completed stock purchase

claims.statement: Commission/Family ballot machinery selects from an approved stock catalog. Safe/registry policy limits assets; the onchain publisher commits server-authoritative results. This is not universal OMR-holder control of the Safe or all economic parameters.
claims.safeNarration: Commission choices operate inside an approved asset list.
claims.safeDepiction: Ballot → APPROVED CATALOG SELECTION. Keep selection visually distinct from purchase confirmation.
publicationBlockers: Verify the production registry generation, ballot result/finality, publisher and acquisition consumer before showing a completed decision-to-buy sequence.
